headline: Elon Musk, chief executive of Tesla and SpaceX, unveiled a Tesla Roadster prototype that used rocket-style thrusters to leap off a ramp, clear five cars and land softly.
score_reason: Pool 7 lowered by 1: the demonstration was on Thursday 15 Oct, before the 16 Oct window, and the car is a prototype with no price or date.
importance_line: A long-promised car shown with a stunt interests Tesla reservation holders and shareholders, but it is a prototype with no price and no date, production is not due before 2028, and the thruster version is not approved for public roads.
summary: NBC News reports that Elon Musk, chief executive of Tesla and SpaceX, showed a prototype of the second-generation Tesla Roadster at a SpaceX test site in Texas on Thursday 15 Oct, where the car drove up a ramp, jumped over five other Teslas and landed softly using cold-gas thrusters (jets of compressed gas), and Tesla says it went from 0 to 60 mph in 0.81 seconds. There is no price or release date and Musk said production would not begin until 2028, while Tesla says the invite-only, single-seat "Rocket" version with the thrusters is not approved for public roads.
notes: Event was Thursday 15 Oct (Texas), reported through 16 Oct; not carried in our 15 or 16 Oct pools, so it is new to our readers. The AP video page was blocked, so NBC News (its own report) is the source. machine_action true because the vehicle is shown launching, flipping and landing; NBC does not say whether it was driven or autonomous.
